title: 2024 AHA/ACC Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
authors: Whelton PK, Carey RM, Aronow WS, et al.
chunk_text: For adults with Stage 2 Hypertension (BP >= 140/90 mmHg) and Chronic Kidney Disease or Diabetes, first-line therapy requires prompt initiation of two antihypertensive agents of different classes. An ACE inhibitor (or ARB) is specifically recommended in CKD patients with albuminuria. Combination with a dihydropyridine CCB (amlodipine) or thiazide-like diuretic (chlorthalidone) achieves optimal 24-hour blood pressure control.

title: IDSA/ATS Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnosis and Treatment of Community-Acquired Pneumonia
authors: Metlay JP, Waterer GW, Long AC, et al.
journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
chunk_text: In adults with severe Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) requiring ICU admission, IDSA guidelines strongly recommend empiric dual coverage with a potent beta-lactam (ceftriaxone 2g IV daily or ampicillin-sulbactam) plus either IV azithromycin (500mg daily) or a respiratory fluoroquinolone (levofloxacin 750mg daily). Routine anaerobic coverage for aspiration is not recommended unless lung abscess or empyema is documented.

title: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2024: Comprehensive Medical Evaluation and Assessment
authors: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
chunk_text: In patients with Type 2 Diabetes and established ASCVD, Heart Failure, or Chronic Kidney Disease (eGFR 20-60 or UACR > 30 mg/g), therapy should include an SGLT2 inhibitor and/or GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven cardiovascular/renal benefit, independent of baseline HbA1c or metformin use. Relaxation of glycemic targets (HbA1c < 8.0-8.5%) is recommended for older adults with severe comorbid conditions.
